thread:
sara: Heads-up: saw ~12% drop in tokens/sec and ~$1.5/M bump in cost after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Opening thread for triage. stack: prod 3.2.1, flashv2 selector change.

infra-bot: deploy-bot rolled out change 1758761200 -> kernel-selector (latency-priority) to eng-runtime pool.

vikram: Can you paste perf numbers? which models, sequence lengths, batch sizes?

sara: model: rw-13b, seq=1024 typical, p99 latency unchanged, p50 improved slightly, but throughput down. Quick summary:
```
before: tokens/sec = 1.23M, $/M = $11.8, KV_hit = 87%
after:  tokens/sec = 1.08M, $/M = $13.3, KV_hit = 72%
avg_effective_batch_size: 1.8 -> 1.45
```

dana: Looks like selector started preferring paged-attn for longer sequences to lower single-request latency. paged-attn reduces per-request memory but increases kernel invocation count and reduces batching headroom. batch_eff dropped ~20%. quick flame counts show higher kernel-entry overhead.

vikram: Can we repro on perf-cluster? Run: `bench/throughput --model rw-13b --seq 1024 --warm 5m --mode a/b` and capture kernel_invocations, effective_batch_size, kv_hit.

sara: Ran a perf-cluster run (sanitized):
```
variant          tokens/sec    ms/token   kernel_inv/s   avg_batch   kv_hit
fused-flash      1.28M         0.78       4200           1.9         86%
flashv2-fused    1.22M         0.81       4600           1.7         84%
paged-attn       1.05M         0.95       6300           1.4         72%
```
Notes: paged-attn reduces tail latency slightly for single requests but kills global throughput and increases $/M due to more kernel calls and lower batching.

dana: Observations: selector change prioritized latency-per-request but didn't account for impact on batch accumulation and KV hit correlation. When kv_hit drops (we saw it drop after recent cache-ttl tweak), paged-attn invokes more kernels and effective_batch_size collapses -> tokens/sec down.

vikram: Proposal: two options:
- quick rollback to previous kernel-selector policy (fast) + run A/B to validate
- change selector heuristic to consider `effective_batch_size` and `kv_hit` (pref fuse when avg_batch > 1.6 AND kv_hit > 80%) and ship as patch (slower)
Which is faster?

sara: I can schedule rollback in 10m if we agree. Rollback will restore throughput to baseline in canary and then prod. Dana, +1?

dana: :thumbsup: rollback + run perf harness. Also add telemetry: kernel_invocations_per_sec, effective_batch_size and kernel_variant per request ID so we can correlate $/M regressions automatically.

infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled rollback 1758770000 -> kernel-selector v1 (latency-priority revert). Will post metric diff snapshot in #eng-runtime in ~15m.
